finding: Possible weak oracle remains: the r-004 fix widens the crash deny-list by two strings instead of adding a positive check per case
why: A reading member that fails the same way on both twins with any other text or exit code (for example rc 2 with 'error: unrecognized arguments', or a quiet rc 1) still passes as parity, so the list needs a new string per failure seen.
fix: Give each Case an expected return code or marker (default 0 for outcome() members) and assert it on the inside value in observe_pairs, as r-004 proposed.

finding: Possible: a developer's `--dir` that climbs out keeps an unnormalized DEST and makes a stray short-name folder
why: The developer branch sets WORKTREE_PARENT to the short-name folder and leaves PLACED false, so DEST is `<root>/<short name>/../x` (not P_TARGET) and `mkdir -p "$WORKTREE_PARENT"` makes the short-name folder (unmarked, empty) when it is missing; the path in WORKTREE_PATH and the owner record keeps the `..` (downstream effect of the `..` not traced; found by reading).
fix: In the developer-refused branch set DEST from P_TARGET (already normalized by placement) and skip making the short-name folder.
evidence: scripts/create-worktree:389 `WORKTREE_PARENT="$P_FOLDER"` with 415 `DEST="$WORKTREE_PARENT/$DIR_NAME"` and 416 `[[ "$PLACED" != true ]] || DEST="$P_TARGET"`; the new test only compares realpaths (`same(path, root / "dv")`)

finding: Possible: the claim now also runs in agent --parent mode with a symlink-resolved folder, so a marked, symlinked short-name folder fails the creation
why: In parent mode placement returns P_FOLDER as realpath(base); claim_short_name_folder compares `e.short_name == folder.name` to that resolved name, so a short-name folder that is a link to a differently named folder skips the fast path, finds no entry and exits 1 with 'could not be made with its marker' (found by reading; not run).
fix: Pass the short name to the claim (or build the folder as `<root>/<short name>` unresolved) instead of deriving it from the resolved folder's basename.
evidence: scripts/create-worktree:410 `[[ "$P_STATE" != inside ]] || CLAIM_FOLDER="$P_FOLDER"`, :348-349 `e.short_name == folder.name`, :353 `"is no longer listed"`; scripts/placement.py:262-263 `base = os.path.realpath(base)` for the parent (check) path only; no test covers a linked folder

finding: Possible gap: D-53's 'claim is skipped without the lock when the marker names this repository' has no test that would fail if the skip broke
why: Every creation test runs with no lock held and a marker present, so a claim that always takes the lock (skip condition broken) still passes; only the lock-held test reaches the claim, and it removes the marker first.
fix: Add a case: listed repository, marker intact, hold rl.safe_write._file_lock(rl.list_file()) while running create --name, assert exit 0 and the worktree lands under <root>/proj.
evidence: scripts/create-worktree:347-350 `held = repo_list._marker_holder(...)` / `if held and any(...): sys.exit(0)`; DECISIONS D-53 'the claim is skipped without the lock when it does'; the only lock test (line 384-392) begins `(root / "proj" / rl.MARKER_NAME).unlink()`

finding: Possible vacuous check: the new `assert in_changes` ('the member wrote nothing under the root') cannot fail for two writing cases
why: The probes for scripts/lavish/inject.py and write_report.py create their own files in the worktree (probe-page.html, COVERAGE.json) before calling the member, so the change set is non-empty whether or not the member wrote anything.
fix: Snapshot after the fixture setup inside the probe, or assert the member's own output file (REPORT.md, the rewritten page) is in in_changes for those two cases.
evidence: test_existing_worktree_outside_root.py:826-827 `page.write_text("<html>...Zorblax...")` before `inject.inject_file`; :789-791 `(folder / "COVERAGE.json").write_text(...)` before write_report.py; observe() takes `before` at :881 ahead of the probe, so probe-written files count as changes
